label: Teltonika RUT281
description: A compact 4G router: 1 WAN + 1 LAN at 10/100, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 4 and an LTE Cat 4 modem. The smallest cellular router in the current line that still has a separate WAN port.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT281 datasheet: 1 x WAN port 10/100 Mbps and 1 x LAN port 10/100 Mbps (IEEE 802.3); 4G LTE Cat 4 up to 150 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up; 802.11b/g/n (Wi-Fi 4) access point and station, modelled at the 300 Mbps 2x2 rate the standard gives. Two Ethernet ports, not a switch.

label: Teltonika RUT286
description: An industrial global 4G router: 1 WAN + 1 LAN at 10/100, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 4, LTE Cat 4 and mesh support. The rugged version of the RUT281.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT286 datasheet: 1 x WAN port 10/100 Mbps and 1 x LAN port 10/100 Mbps (IEEE 802.3); 4G LTE Cat 4 up to 150 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up; 802.11b/g/n (Wi-Fi 4) with AP, station and mesh (802.11s) support, modelled at 300 Mbps. Same port shape as the RUT281, in an industrial case.

label: Teltonika RUT261
description: A two-port industrial router with LTE Cat 6: 1 WAN + 1 LAN at 10/100 and a 300 Mbps modem. Twice the cellular throughput of the Cat 4 two-port units.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUT261 datasheet: 1 x WAN port 10/100 Mbps and 1 x LAN port 10/100 Mbps (IEEE 802.3); 4G LTE Cat 6 up to 300 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up, 3G up to 42 Mbps - modelled at the 300 Mbps class, twice the Cat 4 units. No Wi-Fi is claimed: the only 802.11 reference in the datasheet is 802.11e QoS on the bridge, which is not a radio. If your unit has a radio, that is a gap worth a comment.
